source.title: Platonic Representation Hypothesis on World Models
source.authors: Wenhow Li; Cheng-Wei Ma; Hui Xiong; Ying-Cong Chen; Lei Zhang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests Platonic-style representational alignment in a new setting: world models trained on shared state-transition tasks with heterogeneous visual encoders.
record.gate_note: The paper reports geometric-alignment results, stitching success rates, anchor-sensitivity findings, and later-checkpoint results. It also reports planning rates used to select DINOv2-S as an anchor; those rates are not themselves alignment results and are not rows here. Cited findings from prior work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study trains DINO-WM predictors on frozen encoders (DINOv2-S/B/L/G, SigLIP, MAE, ResNet18) under one shared transition objective. It measures anchored m-kNN alignment of predictor states across training, against other anchors and at later checkpoints, plus planning success of stitched predictors. This is a new setting (world models, five simulated control tasks) with direct results on V1, V4, V6 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a shared transition objective can drive heterogeneous ViT priors toward similar predictor geometry, while the ResNet gap reveals architectural constraints. They say stitching with lightweight MLPs shows functional compatibility among strong planners. They attribute the failures of MAE front-ends in Wall to weak endpoint competence. They limit claims to frozen-encoder DINO-WM on five simulated tasks and treat the anchor as operational.
record.recipe_differences: Uses anchored mutual k-NN and predictor-layer stitching in world models, rather than the original sources' representation comparisons; tests a new world-model setting with transition training.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment scores and some local rankings change with the chosen anchor; the broad ViT-versus-ResNet pattern remains. Alignment also varies by environment and checkpoint, with later curves not monotonically increasing. Stitching SSR depends on split depth, direction, and environment.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-model predictor alignment drops from raw encoder space to predictor epoch 1, then recovers by epoch 10. Within-model encoder–predictor similarity does not generally rise, so the alignment is not inherited input geometry (Figures 5 and 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared-objective training induces cross-model alignment in downstream modules that is not inherited from the similarity of their input encoders.

record.problems: The alignment curves and anchor-sensitivity results are reported as figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The main anchor is selected for planning performance rather than being an independently established ideal. Only frozen-encoder DINO-WM predictors and five simulated tasks are studied. Stitching tables give SSR but not matched unstitched endpoint success rates for each pair and condition, limiting direct assessment of performance loss. No alternative numerical similarity metric or k value is compared.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the reported stitching table. The separate environment-by-model curve values in Figures 3, 8, and 9 and the visual overlays in Figures 4 and 10 are not expanded into one row per plotted point; the retained rows record the paper's reported qualitative comparisons because the plotted values are not stated numerically.

untested.parts: Alignment as a function of model size: DINOv2 S/B/L/G are compared only to a DINOv2-S anchor, with no size trend reported. Also untested: models with different training data or modalities, since all predictors share the environment data and objective.
Entire version: no vision–language paired alignment is measured.
Entire version: no comparison across random seeds.

Linear maps, relative representations and mapping without paired data are untested; stitching uses trained two-layer MLP adapters. ResNet is excluded from stitching, and only PointMaze and Wall are tested.
Entire version: no interpretable features or circuits are studied.
No alternative similarity metric, no variation of k in m-kNN, and no out-of-distribution inputs; only the choice of anchor model is varied.

Causal attribution is untested: all models share data and objective, so a shared objective or data cannot be separated from a common model of reality. Absolute closeness to complete alignment is not quantified in the text.

missing.what: Unstitched epoch-10 planning success rates per model and environment, which serve as the baseline for every stitching row. The reader marked these as not stated, but they are given.
Normalized retention scores (RS) are defined but never tabulated; the text only says many cases reach RS ≥ 0.7.

Authors state that geometric similarity is partly independent of planning proficiency. This bears on V1's link between capability and alignment; Table 1 planning rates are not monotonic with DINOv2 size.
Within-model encoder–predictor m-kNN at epochs 1 and 10: predictors become less encoder-like in Rope and Granular even as cross-model alignment rises.
Text gives MAE Wall unstitched success as 0.66, but Table 1 lists 0.56; the two are inconsistent.

record.verdict_notes: Stitching rows are re-judged against the Table 1 endpoint success rates; the paper does not state which DINOv2 size was stitched, so DINOv2-S is assumed. The anchor was chosen for planning performance, and alignment values for G rows are figure-only with no uncertainty. The reader's V7 label was changed from limits_scope to supports: V7 is a challenge version, and a persistent gap and plateau are what it predicts. Appendix E reports that ResNet trends toward the transformer pattern in PointMaze only; rows_left_out declares this. All models share data and objective, so V7's causal question cannot be resolved here.

versions.untested_parts: Tests training-time alignment among world models with different frozen vision encoders and comparisons among DINOv2 size variants. Does not test whether independently trained models with different objectives, training data, or modalities become more aligned as model size and capability increase.
No paired image-caption alignment between vision and language models is tested.
No comparison across random initialization seeds of the same architecture or analysis of shared features or subspaces across seeds.
Tests layer stitching with trained adapters on PointMaze and Wall. Does not test relative representations or mapping without paired data.
No recurrence of interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits is tested.
Tests sensitivity to anchor choice and environment, but does not compare alternative numerical similarity metrics or vary the number of neighbours.
Reports architectural gaps and non-monotonic alignment over later training. Does not distinguish whether shared objectives, shared data, or a common model of reality causes the observed alignment.
